question: [FREE] Based on the clip, what imaging mode change is being initiated, and why would this help confirm what was seen in real-time imaging?
answer: They are switching from standard 2D viewing to motion mode (M-mode). This provides an objective time-based record to confirm true motion at the interface rather than relying only on subjective real-time appearance.
groundtruth: The operator prepares to change to M-mode to objectively confirm pleural motion that was observed in 2D imaging.
model_prediction:
Based on the video clip, the user is initiating **M-Mode (Motion Mode)**.

In the first part of the clip, we see B-mode (brightness mode) imaging of the lung, where lung sliding is visible at the pleural line. Towards the end of the clip (around the 7-second mark), the user navigates a menu and specifically selects the "M" icon labeled "M-Mode."

**Why this helps:**
M-Mode is used to confirm the presence or absence of lung sliding, which is critical for diagnosing pneumothorax.
*   **Normal Lung:** M-Mode will show the "seashore sign" (parallel lines above the pleura representing the static chest wall, and a granular/sandy appearance below the pleura representing the sliding lung). This confirms normal lung sliding.
*   **Pneumothorax:** If lung sliding is absent, M-Mode will show the "stratosphere sign" (or "barcode sign"), where horizontal parallel lines persist below the pleural line because the visceral and parietal pleura are separated by air and not sliding against each other.
